newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Interpol, postal body sign accord on mail crime.
newsitem.headline: Interpol, postal body sign accord on mail crime.

text.p: The International Criminal Police Organisation, Interpol, on Tuesday signed an agreement with the Universal Postal Union (UPU) to step up the fight against crime committed through the mail.

The accord provides for close cooperation between the two bodies in the fight against drug trafficking, mail bombs, child pornography and pedophile networks as well as mail fraud and money laundering through the post, officials said.

UPU Director-General Thomas Leavey told a news conference after the signing that, as one of the largest employers in the world moving vast quantities of mail and valuables daily, the postal industry was a natural magnet for criminals.

Under the accord, signed by Leavey and the Lyons-based Interpol's Secretary-General Raymond Kendall, the 123-year-old UPU pledged to work with national postal administrations to help them step up anti-crime programmes.

The UPU, a United Nations agency based in Berne, has 189 members. It is currently holding the annual meeting of its Postal Operations Council, the technical and operational body dealing with international postal services.
